name: Ciza
source: Pathfinder #155: Lord of the Black Sands

generalAbilities.name: Hears Heartbeats
generalAbilities.description: The banshee can hear heartbeats within 60 feet (imprecise).

generalAbilities.name: Sunlight Powerlessness
generalAbilities.description: If in direct sunlight, the banshee is slowed 1 and can't use actions that have the attack trait.

defensiveAbilities.name: Vengeful Spite
defensiveAbilities.description:
Trigger A foe critically hits the banshee, or the banshee critically fails their save against a foe's damaging effect.

Effect The banshee lashes back at their tormentor, dealing (4d10+14) Mental Damage damage (Basic DC 38 Will Saving Throw save) and applying the effects of terrifying touch based on the results of the same Will save.

offensiveAbilities.name: Spectral Ripple
offensiveAbilities.description: When a banshee Strides at least 10 feet, they're concealed until the start of their next turn.

offensiveAbilities.name: Terrifying Touch
offensiveAbilities.description: A creature damaged by the banshee's touch that isn't already Frightened must attempt a DC 38 Will Saving Throw save (DC 43 if the attack was a critical hit). If the creature fails its save, it's Frightened 2; on a critical failure, the creature also cowers with fear and is Stunned 4. If the creature is protected against fear by a spell or magic item, the banshee's touch first attempts to counteract the protection effect, with the effect of a 9th-rank Dispel Magic spell.

offensiveAbilities.name: Wail
offensiveAbilities.description:
The banshee unleashes a soul-chilling Wails of the Damned (DC 38). This Wail overcomes Silence and similar effects of 5th level or lower. The banshee can instead use Wail as a three-action activity to overcome such effects of up to 8th level.

The banshee's Wail resonates for 1 round, and any creature that comes within the area during that time must attempt a save against the effect. A creature can't be affected more than once by the same Wail. The banshee can't Wail again for 1d4 rounds.
